definition: HTTP is a request-response protocol for transferring resources, used by browsers and by APIs. A request names a method and a target; a response carries a status code and a body. The protocol itself does not remember the client between requests; any session state is added by the application.
details: GET is for reading and is meant to be safe. PUT and DELETE are meant to be idempotent. POST is the method for actions that are not necessarily either.
Status classes: 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.
examples: A client posting JSON to an API
